title: Best App to Get Brand Deals: What Each Type Actually Pays, and Which to Pick
summary: Compare the best apps to get brand deals by cost, follower requirements, deal type, and payout timing — plus what happens after you accept an offer and how to spot scams.
body_markdown:
## Marketplace Apps: Apply to Posted Campaigns (Collabstr, Insense, and the 3,000-Follower Floor)


Marketplaces provide a visible place to find campaigns and apply, rather than starting every relationship with a cold pitch. The trade-off is eligibility: some opportunities set follower floors, limiting applications from smaller creators. UGC work offers another route, since brands may commission content for their own channels instead of requiring a creator to publish to a large audience.


### Collabstr: Best for Paid One-Off Gigs With Transparent Listed Rates


**Best for:** creators seeking discrete sponsored deliverables with listed pricing. Collabstr presents creator services and campaign opportunities in a marketplace format. Check each listing for deliverables, publication requirements, usage permissions, and payout conditions; a visible rate does not establish what you keep after platform charges.


Compare the requested work with the fee. A short video with limited[usage rights](https://www.reacherapp.com/blog/ugc-usage-rights-what-to-charge-what-to-include-and-how-to-price-in-perpetuity-rights) differs from content a brand can reuse in paid advertising. Confirm the number of revisions and whether the post must appear on your account.


### Insense: Best for UGC-Style Video Briefs and Usage-Rights Add-Ons


**Best for:** creators producing short-form brand content, including UGC a company may publish on its own channels. Review the brief for format, talking points, deadlines, and usage-rights terms. Usage rights describe where and how a brand may reuse your content, so consider them separately from the creation fee.


Access and eligibility depend on the opportunity. Do not assume every brief is open to every audience size or that usage rights are included in the initial payment. Ask for written terms if either point is unclear.


### Pros and Cons of Marketplaces for Creators Under 10,000 Followers


Marketplaces make it easier to find active briefs, and listed requirements help creators decide whether to apply. Follower thresholds can exclude smaller accounts, and an application does not guarantee selection. Brands may choose based on content style, audience fit, product category, or required deliverables.


A strong sample, clear niche, and reliable production process can support an application; UGC assignments may focus on the content itself rather than audience reach.


### What to Do When You're Below Every Marketplace's Follower Minimum


If minimums block access, build a portfolio of product-focused videos and seek UGC briefs that do not require a large personal audience. Create a business email and concise media kit with your niche, sample work, relevant audience details, and contact information. Apply where the brief fits your skills and the terms are clear.


Brand Intelligence is brand-facing research, not a creator application marketplace. It gives brands visibility into competitor brands and creators associated with their sales to inform creator selection. For an individual creator, the next step is a relevant portfolio and a targeted application or pitch.
